---

**Key differences between 64-bit and 32-bit:**

The only differences are in `PPGETTIME` and `PPSETTIME`, and `sizeof(struct timeval)`. This is because `struct timeval` contains fields of type `time_t` and `suseconds_t`, which are 8 bytes each on amd64 (total 16 bytes) but 4 bytes each on i386 (total 8 bytes). The ioctl number encodes the size of the argument struct, so:

| Ioctl | amd64 | i386 |
|---|---|---|
| `PPGETTIME` | `0x80107095` (size=0x10=16) | `0x80087095` (size=0x08=8) |
| `PPSETTIME` | `0x40107096` (size=0x10=16) | `0x40087096` (size=0x08=8) |
| `sizeof(struct timeval)` | 16 | 8 |

All other ioctl numbers, flag values, and IEEE1284 mode constants are identical between the two architectures.

The source file is at `/tmp/ppdev_ioctl.c`, the 64-bit binary at `/tmp/ppdev_ioctl`, and the 32-bit binary at `/tmp/ppdev_ioctl32`.
